source: Curated from IMO meteor shower calendar, NASA eclipse data, and StarWalk 2026/2027 astronomy calendars. Refresh yearly.
location_note: Events are those visible from or notable from Uganda (equatorial latitude 0.3N).

events.title: Total Solar Eclipse
events.description: Totality crosses the Arctic, Greenland, Iceland and Spain. Uganda sees a small partial eclipse — never look directly without proper solar filters.

events.title: Perseid Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Up to ~100 meteors per hour. Best after midnight when the radiant is higher. Moonlight-free viewing this year.

events.title: Partial Lunar Eclipse
events.description: A partial lunar eclipse visible across Europe, Africa and Asia. Uganda gets a good view of the Moon entering Earth's shadow.

events.title: September Equinox
events.description: The Sun crosses the celestial equator. Around the equinox, day and night are nearly equal in length across Uganda.

events.title: Saturn at Opposition
events.description: Saturn is closest and brightest, rising at sunset and visible all night through any telescope from Uganda's equatorial sky.

events.title: Orionid Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Moderate shower (up to ~20 meteors per hour) from Halley's Comet debris. A waning gibbous Moon sets after midnight, leaving darker skies.

events.title: Leonid Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Up to ~15 meteors per hour with occasional bright fireballs. Best in the hours before dawn.

events.title: Geminid Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: The year's most reliable shower — up to ~150 meteors per hour, visible from both hemispheres. A waxing crescent Moon sets early, so skies stay dark.

events.title: December Solstice
events.description: The longest night of the year in the Northern Hemisphere — a classic night for stargazing in Uganda.

events.title: Quadrantid Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Sharp, intense peak of up to ~110 meteors per hour, best observed in the hours before dawn.

events.title: Annular Solar Eclipse
events.description: Annular path crosses South America and the South Atlantic; western Africa may catch a partial phase. Requires proper solar filters.

events.title: March Equinox
events.description: The Sun crosses back over the celestial equator — day and night nearly equal across Uganda.

events.title: Lyrid Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Up to ~18 meteors per hour from Comet Thatcher, occasionally with bright fireballs.

events.title: Eta Aquariid Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Debris from Halley's Comet; up to ~50 meteors per hour in the pre-dawn sky, well placed from equatorial latitudes.

events.title: June Solstice
events.description: Longest day in the Northern Hemisphere; Uganda's skies are nearly identical day-to-day thanks to the equator.

events.title: Total Solar Eclipse — Africa
events.description: Totality crosses North Africa (Morocco to Egypt). Uganda sees a substantial partial eclipse — use proper solar filters only.

events.title: Perseid Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: The classic summer shower, up to ~100 meteors per hour from Uganda's night sky.

events.title: September Equinox
events.description: Another equinox — a fine excuse for an evening of skywatching.

events.title: Orionid Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Halley's Comet debris again — up to ~20 meteors per hour.

events.title: Leonid Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Up to ~15 meteors per hour; watch for bright Earthgrazers near dawn.

events.title: Geminid Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Up to ~150 meteors per hour, one of the best shows of the year in Uganda.

events.title: December Solstice
events.description: The year's longest night in the north — prime stargazing time.
